betterCitation: EITHER keep the wording and cite the edition that prints it: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 13, Of Experience (trans. Charles Cotton, rev. W. Carew Hazlitt, Navarre Society, 1923) [130 characters; vol. 5, about p. 317]. OR keep the 1877 citation and use the 1877 wording: The great and glorious masterpiece of man is to know how to live to purpose; all other things, to reign, to lay up treasure, to build, are, at most, but little appendices and props. (Reeves and Turner, 1877, vol. III, p. 438 or 439).
reason: Translation drift between editions of the same translator. The quoted wording is NOT that of the named 1877 edition. Two independent archive.org scans of the 1877 Reeves and Turner vol. III (essaysofmontaign03mont, title page dated 1877, and essaysofmontaign03mo) both read: The great and glorious masterpiece of man is to know how to live to purpose; all other things, to reign, to lay up treasure, to build, are, at most, but little appendices and props. The A. L. Burt reprint of Hazlitt reads the same. The wording as proposed (The glorious masterpiece of man is to live to purpose; all other things: to reign ... are but little appendices and props) is Hazlitt's LATER revision, found verbatim in the Navarre Society edition, London 1923, vol. 5 (archive.org essaysofmontaign0005unse), which reprints his revised text. Project Gutenberg 3600 labels itself 1877 but carries the later revised text, and the verifier read only that file. The line is real, the locator (III.13) and the Essay tag are right, shipped.js is clean (not shipped, Montaigne 0 of 3, not banned), and the source fits 140; only the pairing of wording and edition is false, and it is fixable either way.
